title: Can't settle even when you're tired?
caption: Restless for no clear reason? The sky's been a bit lively, and patience can feel thin so small hassles may seem bigger. Pause for slow breathing, step outside, or take a short pleasant break when you notice it.
snapshot: Mostly calm conditions with one recent CME and a slight tilt in the field. The background resonance is a little elevated. This often shows up as lower patience and quicker mood shifts for some people.
affects: Mood and patience can be more brittle than usual. Small hassles may feel larger, and restlessness can climb. People sensitive to head pressure or headaches may notice more reactivity.
playbook:
- When irritation flares, step outside for a few deep breaths
- Short, pleasant breaks (tea, sunlight, gentle movement) can shift mood
- Delay tricky conversations until you feel steadier

sections.voiceover: Tired but can't settle? You might notice your patience is thinner than usual and small hassles feel disproportionately annoying — like a low hum under everything that makes you jumpier. The sky's been a bit lively lately (one recent CME and a slight tilt in the field), which can nudge the background resonance up and show up as mood brittleness, restlessness, or extra sensitivity to head pressure. Try this today: When irritation flares, step outside for a few deep breaths.

fb.caption: Tired but can't settle? You might notice your patience is thinner than usual and small hassles feel disproportionately annoying — like a low hum under everything that makes you jumpier. The sky's been a bit lively lately (one recent CME and a slight tilt in the field), which can nudge the background resonance up and show up as mood brittleness, restlessness, or extra sensitivity to head pressure. Why it matters: when reactivity is high, ordinary frictions become escalations, and decisions made in that edge state often land worse than they need to. If you feel irritation rising, pause: step outside, take a few slow breaths, sip something pleasant, or move gently for a couple minutes — and, when possible, delay thorny conversations until you feel steadier. dimming the volume before you try to tune a tricky instrument. Gaia Eyes is keeping an eye on the background so you can pace with a little more ease.
